description: The citation dialect: the <commons-citation> block grammar, normalization, corpus matching, and the record written to commons.citation.candidates. Shared by pkg-r and pkg-py. The source is tests/shared/citations.json; the copy under pkg-r/tests/testthat/fixtures/shared/ is generated by scripts/sync-shared-fixtures.sh. Edit the source and re-run that script.

parse_commons_citation.description: Splits a <commons-citation> body into verbatim evidence and unverified explanation. The grammar is deliberately strict and deliberately not CommonMark: exactly one contiguous run of lines starting with '>' holds the evidence, and every other line is explanation. Zero runs or two separate runs are malformed. There is no lazy continuation and no indented marker, so a line the model wrapped stays explanation and is never verified. Each implementation trims the explanation with its own language's whitespace class, so a trailing U+00A0 survives in R and not in Python. That is accepted: the explanation is never verified, so the difference is cosmetic.

normalize_citation.description: Forgives the ways a faithful quote can still drift from its source: markdown emphasis, typographic quotes and dashes, and reflowed whitespace. Case is never folded, because match_citation is case-sensitive. Each implementation folds whitespace with its own language's regex, which differ on exotic spaces such as U+00A0.

match_citation.description: First match wins, because the corpus is ordered specific before general. Matching is case-sensitive substring containment after normalizing both sides. `expected` is null when nothing verifies, otherwise the label and kind of the entry that did.
match_citation.guard: A quote whose normalized form is shorter than 10 characters never verifies, so a trivial fragment cannot promote an unsupported answer. Only the quote is ever passed here; the model's explanation is never verified.

citation_scan.description:
The streaming scanner that projects a model's text for display. It rewrites a verified <commons-citation> into a <shiny-aside>, drops every other reserved element, and passes the rest through unchanged. Output must not depend on where chunk boundaries fall.
Each case gives a corpus, an input text, the expected output, and the expected candidate verdicts. Three tokens appear in the strings. '{{pad}}' expands to 'pad.char' repeated so that the body of the first <commons-citation> element is exactly 'pad.citation_body_length' characters, which is how the cap cases stay small on disk. '{{split}}' marks a feed boundary and is removed from the input text. '{{aside:N}}' stands for the Nth entry of 'asides' rendered by the reading package, because the two packages differ in the icon URLs they can resolve; every other character of the expected output is pinned exactly.

citation_holdback.description: What each feed() may emit, rather than what the whole stream projects to. Text is emitted as soon as it is known to be safe, and held back only while the buffer's tail could still grow into a reserved literal on the next chunk. Holding back more than that delays a model's words on screen for no reason; holding back less lets a tag split across two chunks reach the display. 'emitted' pins the return of each feed() in turn, and 'flushed' the return of finish().

cases.name: a tail that cannot start a reserved literal is emitted at once
cases.why: Only a suffix that is a prefix of a reserved literal is worth holding.

cases.name: a partial open tag mid-line is emitted rather than held
cases.why: The opening tag only counts at the start of a line, so mid-line this text cannot become one however the next chunk continues it.

cases.name: a partial open tag at a line start is held until it resolves
cases.why: Here the next chunk could complete it, so emitting now would leak a tag.

cases.name: a partial close tag is held anywhere on the line
cases.why: Closing tags are not anchored to a line start, so any position holds.

cases.name: a partial tag that never completes is flushed at end of stream
cases.why: Held-back text is the model's own words until a tag actually forms.
